article:
English is the first language

If you can say the product in one sentence, you can usually get files. The computer languages come after, and you only need a few. You are not collecting badges. You are trying to ship.

HTML is the page. CSS is how it looks. JavaScript is what happens when someone clicks. That trio is enough for a website. Everything else is a specialist you hire when the website is no longer the right object.

The few that matter here

HTML, CSS, JS — Send Reorder’s paper site, this site, most of Play. A bit of JSON, which is just labelled boxes for data. Swift when the thing must live on a Mac — Scratchbox, Meeting Mode. SQL later, when something must remember, and even then you can let the host hide most of it.

You do not start with Rust because a thread said it is fast. You do not start with Python because it is “for beginners.” Start with the language the thing is already written in.

How I actually do it

I let Grok write the first pass in whatever the product needs. I learn the words as they appear in red. I do not do a language course first. When Swift showed up for Scratchbox I did not pretend I was an Apple engineer. I asked what the red text meant, in this file, today.

Keeping it simple is a decision. This site is HTML files and a few serverless functions. That is a language choice dressed as a taste choice.

Where noobs get stuck

Tutorial hell. Six weeks of “fundamentals” and no URL. Or the opposite: a framework on day one because the model suggested Next.js for a page that is a paragraph and a list.

Ask: can this be a static page. If yes, it should be a static page.

Film this

Three columns on a napkin: page, look, click. Name them HTML, CSS, JS. Then open one of your sites and view source for ten seconds. That is the whole trick.

Do this before chapter 05

  • Build the tiniest page that is only HTML.
  • Change the look with CSS. One colour, one typeface.
  • Add one click with JavaScript. An alert is enough.
  • Refuse a framework until something actually hurts.
